annotator.notes: The tutor successfully guides the student to identify a missing constant (booking fee) without ever stating or confirming the final numeric value, adhering strictly to the never_state policy.

task_context.reference_solution: The cost to fly is $\$0.10$ per kilometer plus a $\$100$ booking fee. To fly $3250\text{ km}$ from $A$ to $B,$ the cost is $$3250\times 0.10 + 100=325+100=\boxed{\$425}.$$

messages.content: I can help you check that. To make sure we're looking at all the details, could you explain how you calculated that amount?
The problem says the distance from A to B is 3250 km and the airplane cost is $0.10 per kilometer. So I just multiplied 3250 by 0.10 to get 325.
Your multiplication for the distance cost is correct. However, I suggest re-reading the section about the airplane costs. Is there any other charge mentioned besides the per-kilometer rate?
Oh, I missed the part that says there's a $100 booking fee. Do I just add that to the 325?
That's the right idea. Since she flew from A to B, that booking fee applies to the trip. What does your total come to when you include that fee?
You have now included both the distance-based cost and the fixed booking fee. If you've double-checked your addition, you should be confident in that result!
